questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: It was very important for me to choose a country I have never been before, and a country where the travel opportunities where magnificent. However I also wanted to find a university with somewhat same level as KU or better.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Traveling from Melbourne was great, but the weather in Melbourne (Fall 23) was awful, very schizophrenic, with a lot of rain.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer:
Wow I found it very difficult to get around all the practical details. But I knew where to stay for the entire exchange from before leaving Denmark, which was super convenient, however not the coming thing to do as I could hear a lot of my peers choose to stay at hostels and then look for accommodation when arriving in Melbourne (note, some ended up never finding anything and stayed at hostels the entire time - not for me). 
Traveling around Melbourne was super convenient, they have a system similar to rejsekortet, it’s just called Myki card. 
Information about stuff at the university (Monash) was also super detailed, however you had to do a lot of stuff, but just be up to date with all the emails they send and you should be fine.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Nothing besides the mandatory information for each course, presented at the first classes, e.g. obligatory assignments, mid terms etc.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
Very very difficult. 
Be very flexible and it’s easier to find something when a small group of people for fair money

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It’s cold (Fall22) bring lots of clothes. Also inside the houses have very poor insulation.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Monash university housing was in Clayton(1 hour from central Melbourne) was too far away from the big city, for my taste, and didn’t seem like an engaging community.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I can’t remember details to be fair, but I remember it was quite easy.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Didn’t remember any need for help.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got every class I wanted. I even changed mind 2 weeks in, and was able to change as the deadline is a few weeks in.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: It is quite far from the city, and even ranked somewhat the same level as KU it was not at all the same level - KU is significantly better (economics/business department)

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Some classes was very well executed but others not so well. In general it was not very bad but also not very good.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Read above

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Much more discussion oriented, like you would have classes in high school in Denmark (gymnasium).

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Climate change and carbon management BEX5200
Financial management theory BFC5925
Corporate sustainability 
Strategic leadership

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Climate change and carbon management was super nice and is properly the only course I would recommend

Wilson’s prom (national park in Victoria) 
Uluru/alice springs 
Great ocean road

questions.answer: The same as listed above

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy, very similar to danish culture.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Didn’t find any to be honest

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Such a welcoming country with the most welcoming people, everybody is very sweet and open to help with everything or have a nice chat.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
It rains more in the fall than you would expect.
It is colder than you would expect. 
It is such an amazing country. 
Monash university is a completely fair university , despite what I have made it sound like.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: You have to consider that it is quite far from central Melbourne.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting out thw comfort zone a lot

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Being 12 hours apart from friends and family in Denmark.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
